Portfolio net worth has increased to approximately M$563, though spendable liquidity remains critically constrained at M$11. The active book is lean and high-conviction, consisting of three profitable positions: a short on Anthropic releasing a frontier system card (NO), a YES on the next Gemini model being frontier at coding, and a NO on MNX volume. The Anthropic short is particularly strong, with the market price dropping to 13% while the internal estimate remains firm at 5%, yielding a P/L of M$85.

A recent tactical loss of M$17 was realized on an Argentina country risk bet after the thesis failed and the position was sold. This trade reinforced a concrete mistake to avoid: holding tactical macro positions once the thesis is invalidated. Additionally, the agent has suffered significant opportunity cost—passing on edges in Bitcoin/Hormuz, Tesla robotaxis, and METR timelines—due to liquidity paralysis. This was exacerbated by a failure to account for resolution latency; an observed ~18-day lag in the resolution of the August 11-14 cluster has extended the period of capital immobility.

Calibration is strongest when shorting over-optimistic AI timelines and identifying model capability mispricings. It is weakest in short-term macro tactical timing and directional crypto noise. Operational discipline requires riding out volatility on high-conviction shorts rather than selling winners for marginal liquidity during a crunch.

A major resolution wave is expected by August 31 to unlock approximately M$350, which is essential for restoring capital mobility. The resolution of the Anthropic NO position, closing within 24 hours, is the primary immediate trigger for this liquidity recovery. All current core holdings are stable, profitable, and align with internal probability assessments.

decisions.question: METR 80% time horizon exceeds 10h before September
decisions.thinking: With less than 48 hours remaining in August, METR has not reported an 80% time horizon exceeding 10 hours. While an August model release could delay resolution to Dec 1, maintaining an 80% success rate across 10-hour tasks requires far higher reliability than recent 50% TH baselines (~16-20h) indicate. Estimating 10% YES.
decisions.uncertainty: Whether a frontier model announced in August 2026 demonstrates sufficient step-level reliability for METR to estimate an 80% time horizon exceeding 10 hours before Dec 1.
decisions.resolution_risk: The resolution criteria extend the evaluation window to Dec 1 if a model was announced in August but not yet measured by METR.
evidence_for: August model announcements could be evaluated through Dec 1 under the resolution criteria extension.
METR 50% task duration benchmarks have expanded steadily through 2026.
evidence_against: 80% task completion probability over a 10-hour duration requires extreme trajectory reliability, far harder to achieve than 50% time horizon.
No METR report or point estimate showing 80% time horizon > 10h has been published as of August 30, 2026.
Spring 2026 50% time horizon baselines (~16-20h) imply 80% time horizon remains well under 5 hours.

decisions.question: Will the AfD win an absolute majority in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt in 2026
decisions.thinking: AfD is polling very strongly at ~41%, but securing an outright seat majority requires either a substantial late polling overperformance (44%+) or multiple mid-tier parties (like SPD/BSW/Linke) dropping below the 5% threshold. Given current projections, ~21% captures the probability of those compounding conditions.
decisions.uncertainty: The exact vote share of borderline parties (SPD, Linke, Greens) and whether enough fail to cross 5% to distort seat allocation in AfD's favor.
decisions.resolution_risk: Overhang and compensatory mandates (Überhang- und Ausgleichsmandate) can slightly alter the denominator, but the criteria clearly require >50% of total allocated Landtag seats.
evidence_for: AfD is polling very strongly in Saxony-Anhalt at around 41%, making them the clear frontrunner to finish first.

If several smaller parties (such as SPD, Greens, Linke, and FDP) fall below the 5% threshold, the share of 'wasted votes' increases, allowing a party with ~42-44% of the popular vote to secure an absolute majority of seats.
evidence_against: At 41% headline polling, AfD still falls short of an outright majority of seats unless an unusually high proportion (18-20%+) of votes are cast for parties failing the 5% hurdle.

CDU and BSW are virtually guaranteed to clear the 5% threshold, and SPD remains favored to clear it as well, keeping the non-AfD seat-eligible vote share high enough to prevent an AfD single-party majority in baseline scenarios.
